netinterest-situational-awareness-67-per:
A fund that lost 67% in the month of July is still up 80% for the year.
Both numbers belong to Situational Awareness, the hedge fund built around AI infrastructure names, and both come from the letter it sent its investors.

@@REF@@'We let you down this month': Aschenbrenner's letter to investors (Business Insider, 2026-07-31)|https://www.aol.com/articles/let-down-month-read-leopold-191821000.html|https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/07/31/8f4c92b6-bb26-399f-8e7e-63cfafdf09a0/434abb36-39da-4c34-a2a3-5a05a901409f.jpg

In the letter Aschenbrenner wrote that the fund "came closer to permanent capital impairment than is acceptable to us."
The same letter says a single block transaction stripped out all of the borrowed money, and that every short position was closed.

## Why this fund and not another

Marc Rubinstein explains the episode through three rules Steve Cohen set out in 2021.
Liquidity, leverage, concentration.
One of them you may survive, two is trouble, and all three at once is whistling past the graveyard.

Take them one at a time.
Liquidity is whether you can sell without cutting the price much.
Leverage is how much borrowed money sits on top of your own, and concentration is how few names hold all of it.
When the three overlap, a small drop forces a sale, the sale pushes the price down further, and because it all sits in a handful of names the loss lands in one place.

Rubinstein's account of July runs like this.
The 29 US-listed long positions fell 21% on average over the month, while shorts such as Adobe rose 26%.
With three to four times leverage on top of that, the fund ended the month down 67%.
Strip out unlisted holdings such as Anthropic and he puts the public book down around 85%.

@@REF@@Aschenbrenner's AI hedge fund collapses after margin calls (Quartz, 2026-07-31)|https://qz.com/situational-awareness-hedge-fund-margin-call-citadel-fire-sale-073126|https://qz.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,quality=85,format=auto/https://assets.qz.com/media/GettyImages-2263060506-300x200.jpg

Quartz reports the fund ran borrowed money as high as 400%, and that SK hynix, CoreWeave, Nebius, SanDisk and Micron each fell more than 35% in July.
The size of those falls matters less than the fact that they were not five separate companies so much as five ways of owning the same story. That is what concentration means here.

## How did the market find out

The letter also describes how the market worked out the fund's position.
"As these moves proceeded, we started to see increasingly adverse trading in names publicly associated with us."
Aschenbrenner compared it to a bank run: vulnerability begetting more vulnerability.

Where that list of names came from is not spelled out.
In the US, an institution managing more than $100 million in listed equities has to disclose its holdings every quarter on a form called the 13F.

@@CHK@@13F filings on record|5|Most recent filing date|2026-02-11|Filings since then|none@@The July book cannot be verified from disclosure. The list the market called "this fund's names" came from reporting and inference, not from a filing.@@Retrieved 2026-08-03 · SEC EDGAR (Situational Awareness LP, CIK 0002045724)

Without a confirmed list, the market is likely to guess broadly.
The broader the guess, the wider the set of names that gets sold ahead of the seller.

## Why blown-up managers raise money again

What Rubinstein's piece is really about is not the collapse but what comes after it.
The trader John Arnold used to hold that "the optimal number of past blow ups was one" when hiring.
Someone who has been broken once, in that view, beats someone who never has.

The record points the same way.
Citadel's Ken Griffin was down 55% in 2008 and TCI's Chris Hohn 43% in the same year, and both survived.
After LTCM failed in 1998, the fund John Meriwether started next grew to $2.7 billion.

@@CMP@@The common reading|No one hands money back to a manager who lost 67% in a month. A hit like that ends a career.|Rubinstein's reading|The record shows managers who blew up large raised fresh capital with relative ease. The market counts the experience as something closer to a credential.
The split is whether you read the same event as a failure or as tuition paid.

The precedent Rubinstein calls the closest fit, though, is not a comeback story.
It is Amaranth Advisors, twenty years ago.
That fund was also shopped to several buyers before Citadel took it on,
and its star trader was two years into the job.

A month before the collapse, the Wall Street Journal sent a reporter to his home for a profile.
Aschenbrenner was profiled by the same paper in June.

The fund that Amaranth's trader started next drew $800 million of commitments and never got off the ground.

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Whether this was one manager's accident, or a structural problem with all the money crowded into AI infrastructure names.

What settles it is the record without leverage.
The fund says it will now run its public book on a fully-paid-for basis.
If the same names hold up from here, July's fall was made by borrowed money. If they slide anyway, the problem was the selection.

67% and 80% are the same fund in the same year.
Losing two thirds of the capital in a month and still sitting above where the year started tells you how much it had been making until then.
Borrowed money multiplies the rate of gain and the rate of loss by the same factor.

The "600,000 a month" counted below is the number of round silicon discs the chips on that stick are printed from.|Smial · FAL 1.3|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DDR5_SDRAM_(with_scale)_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg

## How big is 600,000 wafers

A wafer is the round silicon disc chips are printed on.
The size of a fab is measured by how many of those discs it can start in a month.

Tom's Hardware laid out this year's estimates from Citrini Research.
For 2026 they put CXMT at 350,000 a month, Micron at 375,000, SK hynix at 590,000 and Samsung at 720,000.

@@REF@@CXMT close to matching Micron's memory capacity in 2026, research claims (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-15)|https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/dram/cxmt-close-to-matching-microns-memory-capacity-in-2026-research-claims-would-put-china-on-track-to-become-worlds-second-largest-dram-producer|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3nVy6PgRqeCbLk2BiLxR5W-1920-80.jpg

Drop the 600,000 Reuters describes onto that table and the position is clear.
The fabs already under construction are enough to put a Chinese company on the same line as SK hynix.
The Beijing fab being discussed now would sit on top of that.

## Can $8.9 million build a fab

Reuters puts the cost of a leading-edge 12-inch DRAM fab at more than $10 billion.
The $8.9 million being sought from the local government is under 0.1% of that.

So it is more natural to read the money as something other than construction funding.
It looks closer to a sign that the district has taken the project on as its own, securing land, permits and the slot where much larger money arrives later.
The same report says CXMT already runs a fab in Yizhuang with capacity of about 100,000 wafers a month.

## Do more discs mean more supply

One thing is left.
Wafer count and the memory capacity that actually reaches the market are not the same statement.
The finer the circuits, the more chips come off a single disc, and the more capacity each chip holds.

This is where China is blocked.
Barred from buying ASML's most advanced lithography machines, its makers work around the limit with older DUV tools, and that ceiling already showed up once in the speed of the LPDDR6 CXMT produced.

@@CMP@@The oversupply reading|600,000 a month is SK hynix scale. Pour that into commodity DRAM and prices break first.|The reading that separates discs from bits|If each disc yields less capacity, doubling the disc count does not double the gigabytes that reach the market.
Both readings agree that pricing takes pressure. What splits them is when the pressure arrives and which products it reaches.

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Whether this marks the point where China's DRAM volume push began, or is still talk at the planning stage.

Two things settle it.
Whether the Beijing fab actually breaks ground, and whether what comes out of Shanghai and Hefei stays in commodity DDR5 and LPDDR or climbs into high-specification server parts.

Reuters carried this on sources, and did not say the company had confirmed it.
Plans at this stage sometimes arrive as described and sometimes disappear quietly.
The two earlier fabs, though, are already being built, so the 600,000 figure is not a plan. It stands on construction sites.
jukan-samsung-foundry-100-utilization-2n:
Samsung's foundry division is targeting 100% utilization within the second half of this year.
Utilization is currently estimated at 70 to 80%, and industry accounts say the order backlog and the state of contract talks make hitting that target all but certain.
Lines that sat below 50% from 2024 would be full again after roughly a year.

@@REF@@Samsung Electronics Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results (Samsung Newsroom, 2026-07-30)|https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-second-quarter-2026-results|https://img.global.news.samsung.com/global/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/29111731/Samsung-Corporate-More-Stories-Second-Quarter-2026-Reults_Thumb932.jpg

That release is as far as the company itself has gone.
It says only that foundry earnings improved significantly on HBM base-die demand and strong orders from US customers. There is no utilization figure and no date for a return to profit.
Foundry results are also folded into the DS division alongside memory, so there is no way to check from outside whether the business has crossed into profit.

## Why does utilization matter so much
Utilization is the share of a plant's capacity that is actually running.
Think of a restaurant and how many of its seats are filled. Half-empty or full, the rent and the staff cost the same.

Contract chipmaking takes this much further because of how much capital sits in the equipment.
Depreciation runs whether the lines move or not, which is why the foundry could not even cover fixed costs last year when 4nm and 5nm utilization fell below 50%.
Run the same lines closer to full and the extra revenue drops almost straight to profit.

## So why say 2028
In a June briefing, foundry head Han Jin-man put annual profitability at 2028.
His reason was that turning one profitable quarter is not the same as finishing a year in the black.

@@REF@@Samsung Foundry Chief Sets 2028 for Annual Profit, Tempering Talk of a 2026 Rebound (Tech Times, 2026-06-14)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318311/20260614/samsung-foundry-chief-sets-2028-annual-profit-tempering-talk-2026-rebound.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/466638/amsung-electronics-factory.jpg

The same article lists the reasons he gave for the losses.
Legacy businesses being wound down, newly introduced performance bonuses, technology that is not yet mature enough, low-margin orders, and the delayed ramp of the Taylor fab in Texas.
Higher utilization does not make those items disappear.

## Where is the real threshold
This is where the industry splits.
Some argue the watershed for full-scale orders from large customers such as Qualcomm and AMD is not 100% utilization but whether 2nm yields clear 70%.

Yield is the share of chips on a wafer that come out working.
When yield is low, the same wafer produces more scrap, so the cost of each usable chip stays high even with the lines running flat out.
Utilization tells you how full the line is; yield tells you how much of what comes off it can be sold.

The original post's point that yield comes first holds up in the numbers.@@Retrieved 2026-08-03, citing TrendForce (2026-04-14) and Tech Times (2026-06-14) reporting

@@REF@@Samsung 2nm Yields Reportedly at ~55%, Below Mass Production Threshold; Qualcomm May Opt for TSMC (TrendForce, 2026-04-14)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/04/14/news-samsung-2nm-yields-reportedly-at-55-below-mass-production-threshold-qualcomm-may-opt-for-tsmc/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/04155736/Samsung-20260304-624x413.jpg

## What settles it
The question comes down to one thing. Is 100% utilization the finish line for profitability, or a waypoint with one threshold still ahead.

If the non-memory business turns a quarterly profit in Q3 or Q4 and 2nm yields settle in the 70% range, the first reading is right.
If the lines fill while yields stay in the 60s, the Qualcomm case repeats and large customers keep taking full production elsewhere.

Much of the volume filling those lines was created by the memory boom.
For the lines to stay full once that boom cools, outside customer names will have to fill the space instead.
jukan-rtx50-korea-price-hike-memory-cost:
Prices for NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 50 series in South Korea rise by up to 30% starting this month.
What pushed them up is not a performance upgrade or a new launch. It is component cost.

@@REF@@GeForce RTX 50 Prices Could Jump Another 30% as Memory Crunch Deepens (ThinkComputers, 2026-07-31)|https://thinkcomputers.org/geforce-rtx-50-prices-could-jump-another-30-as-memory-crunch-deepens|https://thinkcomputers.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/rtx-5080-2025-1.webp

That report shows this is not only a Korean story.
It says NVIDIA may raise graphics card prices by a further 20 to 30% during 2026, with the increase landing in the weeks or months after partner inventory sells through.
Korea's increase this month looks like the same schedule arriving early.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|A graphics card. The large chip in the middle is the graphics processor, and the smaller chips ringing it are the memory that just got more expensive.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

## Why is there memory on a graphics card
A graphics processor has to pull the data it draws with at very high speed.
So the board carries several dedicated memory chips around the processor, and that memory is called GDDR.

It shares its roots with the DRAM you plug into a desktop.
The design is simply tilted toward moving a lot of data at once.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg/960px-DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg|A DRAM stick for a desktop. The GDDR on a graphics card comes off the same production lines, which is why it moves with DRAM prices.|Smial · FAL 1.3|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DDR5_SDRAM_(with_scale)_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg

Same process, same fabs. That is the heart of what is happening.
When a memory maker gives more of its lines to server parts, the volume headed for gaming parts shrinks, and what is left gets repriced.

## How much more expensive

@@CHK@@GDDR7 3GB module|$60 to $70|GDDR6 2GB module|about $20|Per gigabyte|about $22 for GDDR7 against about $10 for GDDR6@@The GDDR7 used by the RTX 50 series costs roughly twice as much per gigabyte as the previous generation. Several of these modules sit on a single card, so doubling the module price enlarges memory's share of the card's cost by the same order.@@Retrieved 2026-08-03, citing ThinkComputers (2026-07-31), originally sourced to Economic Daily News

What rose here is not the price of a finished card but the price of one part inside it.
Same model, same performance, different price tag.

## Who raised the price
NVIDIA sells few finished cards itself. It hands board makers a kit that bundles the graphics processor with the memory.
It has reportedly told those partners that the kit price is going up.

@@REF@@NVIDIA is reportedly increasing the prices of its GeForce RTX GPUs due to rising memory costs (TweakTown, 2026-07-23)|https://www.tweaktown.com/news/112801/nvidia-is-reportedly-increasing-the-prices-of-its-geforce-rtx-gpus-due-to-rising-memory-costs/index.html|https://static.tweaktown.com/news/1/1/112801_2_nvidia-is-reportedly-increasing-the-prices-of-its-geforce-rtx-gpus-due-to-rising-memory-costs_full.jpg

That report adds that the increase covers not only the GDDR7-based RTX 50 series but the older GDDR6-based RTX 3060.
So this is not a charge attached to new products. It is attached to any card that uses memory.
Cooling parts and boards are said to have become more expensive as well.

## Who really sets this price
It starts with where a memory maker points its lines.
As long as server DRAM and HBM keep selling for more, gaming GDDR waits its turn.

So a graphics card's price follows the direction of memory prices more closely than it follows NVIDIA's pricing policy.
The shopper sees a price tag on a card, but the hand moving that tag is at a memory supply negotiation.

## What settles it
The question comes down to one thing. Is this increase a price that comes back down once the crunch eases, or one that settles in.

If output from the capacity memory makers have added starts arriving and server demand takes a breather, the first reading is right.
If the added output keeps going to server customers first, gaming card prices stay where they have moved to.

The AI build-out is usually discussed in units of data centres and power.
One of the earliest points where that spending reaches a household budget is this month's graphics card price tag.
macro-week-2026-08-02:
Eight numbers from last week's Kobeissi Letter, lined up in a row.
Apart they are separate stories. Side by side they point the same way.

Global household net worth reached a record $570 trillion in 2025, up 7.3% in a year.
Equities produced 57% of that increase, real estate just 15%.

@@CHK@@Global household net worth (2025)|$570 trillion|Share of the increase from equities|57%|Share from real capital formation|20%@@The $570 trillion is $40 trillion more than a year earlier. McKinsey writes that only 20% of that increase came from actually building anything, while close to 60% came from asset prices rising faster than inflation. Between 2000 and 2024 real estate produced more than half of wealth growth. Last year equities took that place.@@Retrieved 2026-08-03 · McKinsey Global Institute, The Global Balance Sheet 2026 (published 2026-07-23, 2025 data)

@@REF@@The global balance sheet 2026: Imbalance and divergence (McKinsey Global Institute, 2026-07-23)|https://www.mckinsey.com/mgi/our-research/the-global-balance-sheet-2026-imbalance-and-divergence|https://www.mckinsey.com/~/media/mckinsey/mckinsey%20global%20institute/our%20research/the%20global%20balance%20sheet%202026%20imbalance%20and%20divergence/the%20global%20balance%20sheet%202026-1002127418-medium-thumb-1536x1536.jpg

The same report puts the entire global balance sheet near $1.8 quadrillion.
Put simply, the world got richer last year not by making more things, but because the things it already owned were marked higher.

## Who did that wealth land on

If equities made the wealth, it landed on whoever holds equities.
The top 1% of US earners own 50.1% of US stocks and mutual funds, up from 40.1% in 1990.
The bottom half of earners own 1.1%.

Across investors as a whole the tilt is also at a record.
Equities are 65% of the assets held by US households, pension funds, insurers and funds, eight percentage points above the dot-com peak.

## Meanwhile the support underneath is thinning

The rest of the week's numbers run the other way.

The US personal saving rate fell to 2.7% in June, the lowest since June 2022 and a fifth straight monthly decline.
The 2014 to 2019 average was 5.5%. Assets grew while the share of income households keep halved.

Borrowed money is shrinking too.
Margin debt across Korea, China and Taiwan is down $67 billion from its June peak.
Korean leveraged ETFs tied to SK Hynix and Samsung have lost 63% of their assets.

@@REF@@Korea's Leveraged Chip Trade Hits the Margin Call Wall (Investing.com, 2026-07-16)|https://www.investing.com/analysis/koreas-leveraged-chip-trade-hits-the-margin-call-wall-200684082|https://i-invdn-com.investing.com/redesign/images/seo/investingcom_analysis_og.jpg

That analysis reports margin calls on 1.2 million leveraged retail accounts by July 13, with 320,000 to 360,000 liquidated outright.
The leverage came down closer to being forced out by falling prices than to investors changing their minds.

Hedge funds moved the same way, selling global tech stocks over three days into July 28 at the fastest pace since records began in 2016.

## Which way is the price of money going

The last two numbers are close to the answer.

The market puts a record 60% probability on a quarter-point hike at the September FOMC. A hike, not a cut.
Central banks bought a net 289 tonnes of gold in the second quarter, 62 tonnes more than a year earlier and the largest quarterly addition since Q4 2024.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Gold_bullion_bars.jpg/960px-Gold_bullion_bars.jpg|Gold bars. Central banks added 289 tonnes in a single quarter, an asset sitting on the opposite side of price-driven wealth.|Stevebidmead · CC0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gold_bullion_bars.jpg

Borrowing is being priced to get more expensive, and central banks are stacking the one asset that does not depend on a market marking it up.

## So what settles this

The question comes down to one thing.
Is last year's $570 trillion wealth that asset prices can keep producing, or wealth on paper that a single round trip in prices erases.

The place to look is the saving rate and margin balances.
If saving rises and margin debt rebuilds while prices are depressed, households absorbed the assets with their own money.
If saving stays near 2% while margin debt keeps falling, both sources of support left at once.

Wealth rising and money rising are not the same sentence.
A fifth of last year's $570 trillion was newly created. The rest was price.
meru-china-duv-ssa800-1950i-class:
The immersion scanner China says it has built sits at the same level as the NXT:1950i, a tool ASML released in 2008.
It prints 28nm circuits in a single exposure, and the generation above it, the 2015 model 1980Di, is still out of reach.

When a state-backed firm in Shanghai was reported on July 27 to have started volume production of the tool, ASML shares closed down 5.7% and fell as much as 7% intraday.

@@REF@@China begins mass production of homegrown immersion DUV machines, first units to SMIC, Hua Hong and CXMT this year (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-27)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/china-begins-mass-production-of-domestic-immersion-duv-lithography-machines|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/7ZotSVaMnrDA7FNSEBa4BN-970-80.jpg

Tom's Hardware reports the tool prints 28nm-class features in one exposure and reaches 7nm-class when exposures are layered on top of each other.
Deliveries run to about five units this year and roughly 20 next year.

## Why a 2008 model of all things

A scanner is the machine that writes circuits onto a wafer with light.
That single step eats 60% of the time and 35% of the cost of making a chip.

Start with the light itself. The domestic source built by Keyihongyuan runs at 6kHz and 60W.
ASML's part delivers 90W at the same frequency.

For the optics, Maolai is said to have passed validation on a 300mm large-aperture lens.
Its precision lands around 30nm, against under 10nm for Germany's ZEISS lenses, so ZEISS lenses were reportedly imported in the end.

@@REF@@China's DUV lithography still lags ASML by four generations (Asia Times, 2026-07-31)|https://asiatimes.com/2026/07/chinas-duv-lithography-still-lags-asml-by-four-generations/|https://asiatimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/SSA800.jpg

Asia Times names the tool the SSA800 and reports it was built by Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group, founded in 2023, which absorbed development teams from Yuliangsheng and SMEE.
Roughly 70% of the parts are domestic, while mirrors for the 193nm excimer laser, ZEISS lenses, vacuum chambers and synchronization control algorithms are still imported.
Turn that 70% around and it says 30% has to be bought from outside before the machine can be built at all.

## Why the 1980Di could not be copied

Huawei already held the generation above.
HSMC in Wuhan brought in an ASML 1980Di for a 7nm fab and then went bankrupt, and the Chinese government took over the company and handed it to Huawei.

In October 2025, China asked ASML to repair that machine.
The engineer who went on site reportedly found it taken apart and never put back together.

Calibration is what stands in the way.
It is a precision setting that aligns the lenses, mirrors and wafer stage down to the nanometer, fixed at the factory over weeks against hundreds of reference points.
Opening the machine throws that alignment off, and the software key that restores it sits only with ASML.

Even holding the finished product, you lose it the moment you look inside.

## What ASML actually stands to lose

China moved fast because of the calendar.
EUV was blocked from 2019, the NXT:2000i and above from late 2023, and the 1970i and 1980i from September 2024.
Ninety units of the 1980i were stockpiled just before the rules landed, but servicing that lifts performance by more than 1% was banned too, which made upkeep hard.

@@CHK@@ASML China share of sales, H1 2026|about 16%|ASML Q2 2026 net sales|EUR 9.3bn|ASML Q2 2026 net income|EUR 2.9bn@@The market China wants to win back with a domestic tool has already shrunk to about a sixth of ASML's sales. Export controls cut that share first, so what ASML newly loses if localization works is smaller by the same amount. The number points the same way the author does.@@Retrieved 2026-08-03 · sales and net income from ASML's Q2 2026 results release, China share as reported by Tech Wire Asia

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Whether this is the first crack in ASML's moat, or a detour that export controls forced open.

The generation is what settles it.
While the tool stays at 1950i class, it is a detour.
The moment a 1980Di-class machine comes out of domestic parts alone, it is a crack.

ASML took seven years to move from 28nm to 7nm.
There is no visible reason the side walking that road again on a domestic light source and domestic lenses gets less time than that.
A scanner is the one seat in the chip supply chain with no substitute, and whoever holds it is what gives export controls their leverage.
That this tool sits at 2008 level says the leverage is still there.

To push the yen up you have to sell dollars and buy yen.

The money Japan spends on the exchange rate comes out of a special account run by its Finance Ministry.
The account holds $1.3747 trillion, and $1.0087 trillion of it, most of what can be turned into cash quickly, sits in US Treasuries.

Put simply, Japan's dollar wallet is stuffed with US government debt.
Opening the wallet means selling those bonds, and the moment they are sold there are more of them around, so prices fall and yields rise.

The timing matters.
The Korea Exchange opens its regular session at nine.
Nextrade, which opened in 2025 as a second venue where the same Korean stocks can be bought and sold, runs its own pre-open session from 8:00 to 8:50.

So that single share filled during the thinnest hour of the Korean trading day.
One price printed in a window with almost no buyers and no sellers became the reference for the day.

## Who was reading that price

There are places outside Korea where people bet on SK hynix.
They trade perpetual futures, futures with no expiry date.
Nothing changes hands. You are only betting on up or down, so a market can be opened anywhere, whatever exchange the stock is actually listed on.

One of the places where such markets are opened is Hyperliquid.
It is not an exchange run by a company with staff, but a program written in advance that executes its own rules.

Whoever opens a market is a separate party.
The SK hynix market was opened by trade.xyz, and trade.xyz also chose where its price would come from.
What it chose was Nextrade.

## The line where a 5% drop closes you out

One of the rules the operator set was leverage of up to ten times.
A million won of your own money can carry a ten million won bet.

Leverage comes with a line called maintenance margin.
Once your money falls below that line the venue does not wait, it closes the position there and then.
At ten times leverage that line sits around 5%, so a 5% fall is enough to start liquidations.

The reference price fell from $1,127.90 to $917.25, about 18.7%.
At a venue that cuts you off at 5%, an 18.7% fall left only one outcome.

The safeguard trade.xyz had in place allowed a 10% move at once, plus one reset, capping the fall at about 19%.
Because the actual move stayed inside that band, the team says the safeguard worked as designed.

Working as designed is not the same as nothing having happened.

Opening a market requires staking 500,000 HYPE with Hyperliquid, worth about $27.4 million.
Validators can vote to burn that stake.
The burnt money, however, does not go to the traders who lost.

This time trade.xyz said it would fully compensate the losses from the forced liquidations and would fix the way it calculates its price.

Whether this was one operator's configuration problem, or something markets built this way will keep carrying.

Beyond the border, the same price closed out 960 accounts in two minutes.
Where a stock is listed and how far its price travels are now two different questions.

TechTimes traces the gap to how the circuits get printed.
SK hynix prints in a single pass with extreme-ultraviolet tools at a 13.5 nanometer wavelength, while CXMT layers several passes with deep-ultraviolet tools at a longer wavelength.

Layering passes means aligning the plate again each time, and a little misalignment accumulates with every pass.
That accumulated error shaves the top speed the finished circuit can hold.
The ceiling gets cut off during the sorting step, where finished parts are binned by the speed they actually reach.

China has not been able to bring in a single extreme-ultraviolet tool.

The question comes down to one thing.
Whether this is progress on the way to matching the standard, or a ceiling that stops just below its top.

The next generation settles it.
If 12,800 climbs to 14,400 within LPDDR6, multi-pass printing can reach the top after all, and if roughly the same 11% survives into the next generation, that is where the ceiling is.

Chinese memory has taken the route of entering on price and climbing toward the standard.
This number is the first time that road has been measured to the decimal.
It is also how the phrase "lithography is the last bottleneck" ends up written into a product spec sheet.

## Why the three sit in the same kind of seat

The three dissenters have something in common.

The rate-setting committee seats seven governors nominated by the president alongside five regional presidents who rotate into a vote.

## The press conference is what changed

The more important part of the day was not the vote but the press conference.
Chair Kevin Warsh's thinking fits into one line.

If the Fed does not pre-announce its decisions or hint at direction, markets will price their own read of the economy rather than the Fed's words.

That is a decision not to give forward guidance.
Forward guidance means the central bank telling you in advance what it intends to do with rates.
Ben Bernanke reached for it in 2008, when the rate could not go lower, as a way of pulling future cheap money into the present.

Since then the chair's press conference after each meeting has been where you read the next move.
Take that away and there is less reason to listen.

Remove the pre-announcement and the raw material for prices changes.

Whether removing the pre-announcement is a normalisation that pushes markets back to the data, or a retreat that only adds volatility.

If rate futures swing harder than they used to when inflation or jobs numbers land, the cushion guidance used to provide is gone.
If instead the stretches between meetings get quieter, markets really have started pricing the economy rather than the chair.

@@REF@@China adds 14 European entities to export control list, hitting back at EU sanctions (South China Morning Post, 2026-07-24)|https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3361732/china-adds-eu-entities-export-control-list|https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/og_image_scmp_generic/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/07/24/d022c2a5-2adf-4b18-a1da-adb698cbac9b_bab31045.jpg?itok=rXr-fttX&v=1784880870

The South China Morning Post reports the list includes Germany's defence group Rheinmetall, the Italian electric motor maker Lafert and the French drone firm Cavok UAS.
China's commerce ministry called the EU's action egregious and named it directly as the reason for the controls.

## Why the defence industry specifically

The list makes the target obvious.
Rheinmetall is the fastest growing German defence company of Europe's rearmament period.

Dual-use goods are exactly what the name says, items used in civilian life and by the military alike.
Specialist optics, lasers, electric motors, and the rare earths that go inside them all qualify.
Put simply, what has been closed off is not weapons but the materials and parts you cannot build weapons without.

@@REF@@China hits Europe's defence industry in response to the EU's 21st sanctions package against Russia (OSW Centre for Eastern Studies, 2026-07-27)|https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/analyses/2026-07-27/china-hits-europes-defence-industry-response-to-eus-21st-sanctions|https://www.osw.waw.pl/sites/default/files/logo_osw_300_b.png

The OSW Centre for Eastern Studies reads this as Beijing's most direct and forceful response yet to an EU sanctions listing.
The sanctions were meant to stop goods flowing to Russia. What came back was the supply Europe needs for its own weapons production.

## Why this kind of answer is available

A bridge is needed here.
Sanctions work where the other side depends on you, and the reverse holds just as firmly.

Europe's grounds for sanctioning those Chinese firms was that they ship goods onward to Russia.
The original piece cites studies estimating that up to 90% of sanctioned goods still reaching Russia pass through China.
That is a measure of how much of the channel Beijing holds.

But building weapons in Europe requires materials that come from the country holding that channel.
The side you can sanction and the side that can sanction you back are the same country.

## Checkers and chess

This is where the original's title metaphor lands.
Chess is a game where you work out how your opponent answers before you commit to a move.
Playing the move in front of you without counting the reply is closer to checkers.

When the sanctions list was drawn up, was anyone counting whether the other side could answer with the identical move, and what Europe would find itself short of when it did?
The reply that arrived the next day is asking whether that arithmetic was done.

## So what will tell us which it was

In the end the question is one.
Whether this counter-move is positioning for a negotiation, or a real constraint on European defence production schedules.

The place to look is delivery dates.
If Rheinmetall and other European defence firms push back delivery schedules, or announce alternative sources, it was a real constraint.
If months pass with production plans unchanged, it was closer to positioning.

A sanctions list is a list of what the other side depends on you for, and at the same time a list of what you depend on them for.
Read only one of the two and you get an answer back the next day, as happened here.

UPI reports that the 9.2% drop in energy goods was the largest since August 2022.
What pushed the index negative for a month, in other words, was energy rather than prices in general.

The reason markets cheered the number sits two days earlier, at the Fed meeting.
Rates were held 9 to 3, and all three dissents were for a hike rather than a cut.
Data showing prices cooling takes the wind out of the side arguing for higher rates.

## Why the Fed does not watch the CPI

Here is the part that snags.
The number we call inflation in the news is usually the consumer price index, the CPI.
But the yardstick the Fed measures its 2% target against is not the CPI. It is the personal consumption expenditures price index, the PCE.

The two are built differently.
The CPI fixes more than a hundred thousand items into a basket and prices that basket.
The PCE keeps changing what is in the basket according to what people actually bought.

When beef gets expensive, households buy more chicken.
A fixed basket cannot follow that move, so it charges the full beef increase to the index.
That failure to see shoppers switching to whatever got cheaper, which makes measured inflation run high, is called substitution bias.

## Why this statistic was a political problem

The homework in front of Congress in 1995 was the deficit.
More than half of federal spending was mandatory, programs like Social Security, and both those increases and the income tax brackets were indexed to the CPI.

Indexed means one CPI print moves spending and tax revenue at the same time.
So a finding that the CPI overstated inflation changed the arithmetic.
It would slow the growth of outlays without anyone having to vote to cut pensions.

The commission Congress set up delivered its verdict on December 4, 1996.
The CPI was overstating inflation by about 1.1 percentage points a year, and substitution bias was the largest single piece of it.

@@REF@@Final Report of the Advisory Commission to Study the Consumer Price Index (US Social Security Administration archive, 1996-12-04)|https://www.ssa.gov/history/reports/boskinrpt.html

The report itself spells out why a statistic was a money question.
If the CPI overstated the cost of living by one percentage point a year for a decade, the report calculated, the resulting addition to the deficit would reach roughly $135 billion by 2006, making it the fourth largest federal program behind Social Security, health care and defense.

The Fed's official yardstick changed from CPI to PCE in February 2000.

## Does that yardstick really read lower

That holds as a long-run average, but June ran the other way. Energy prices fell hard, and energy carries more weight in the CPI, so the CPI came down further. Strip out food and energy and the gap widens to 0.7 points in the same direction. For this month alone, the number the Fed uses was the stricter one, not the softer one.@@Retrieved 2026-07-31 · US Bureau of Labor Statistics June CPI (released 2026-07-17) · US Bureau of Economic Analysis June PCE (released 2026-07-30)

The effect of swapping yardsticks is not the kind of thing a single month confirms.
Averages running lower and this month running lower are different claims, and this month was inverted.

## How we will know

In the end there is one question.
Is this cooling the start of a trend, or a one month energy effect.

The place it splits is oil.
What pulled June down was the drop in crude that came out of a temporary truce with Iran, and in July that truce broke and crude is rising again.
If energy turns positive again in the July print, June was a one month affair. If core prices, with food and energy stripped out, keep coming down alongside it, the trend reading holds.

The side that changed the yardstick and the side that asked for the change each had their own arithmetic.
The Fed got a target that is easier to hit, and Congress got a way to shrink the deficit without losing votes.
It is worth knowing how the number markets are cheering today was chosen.

## What X-FAB actually makes

A foundry builds chips on behalf of whoever designed them.
The best known ones make the phone and AI chips at the leading edge. X-FAB is not that.

This company makes analog and power semiconductors.
Chips that switch electricity on and off and change its direction, chips that turn light and sound into electrical signals.
Its main customers are automotive and industrial equipment, and those markets are weak right now.

That is where the revenue decline sits.

## So what got confirmed

@@REF@@X-FAB Q2 2026 slides: recovery signals emerge despite revenue decline (Investing.com, 2026-07-30)|https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/xfab-q2-2026-slides-recovery-signals-emerge-despite-revenue-decline-93CH-4825806

Separate from the results, the release carried three things.

Silicon carbide is a material that withstands higher voltages than silicon.
As data center power distribution moves up to 800 volts, conventional silicon parts struggle and this material gets used instead.
The company naming that transition as a tailwind for its own business is what this release contained.

Photonics sits in the same place.
When the links between servers move from copper to light, someone has to build the chips that handle that light, and X-FAB puts its production at 2028.

## The income statement and the thesis are in different years

The second-quarter numbers were made by automotive and industrial equipment.
The design wins and the 2028 date are a data center story.

A design win is not revenue.
It is a customer committing to build a chip on your process, and it usually takes two to three years before that chip actually sells.
So this quarter's figures and this quarter's news point at different years.

The question comes down to one thing.
Whether the current weakness is the cost of crossing a transition, or a sign that this company's share of the new demand is small.

2027 settles it.

Third-quarter guidance is $195 million to $205 million with an EBITDA margin of 17% to 20%.
That looks above this quarter's 16.8%, so whether a recovery has started shows up first in the next set of numbers.
